output.brief: The wrong dates did not come from the operators or the printer firmware. Printer job records show that from 4 Oct the line system sent a 36-month shelf life instead of 24. No operator overrode it, and the camera only checks the print against that same job data, so it passed every carton. On 3 Oct Regulatory Affairs entered 36 months for Veltranol in the ERP, but only to take effect from 1 Mar 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. PackBridge appears to have used the future value anyway. That contradicts the vendor's claim, and the reason is still unexplained. Two Veltranol lots from Line 1 day shift (permanent staff) are also affected and are in the warehouse. Jobs before 4 Oct were correct, so it is not an older problem. Don't warn or remove the agency operators. Don't switch off the camera check. Do this next: fix the Veltranol shelf-life records, and hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two on Line 1. Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at every setup. Check retained cartons of products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30, MR-05-14). Ask Corvane to explain why a future-dated value was sent. Wait on a 12-month reconciliation and on over-labelling other products until those checks come back. I'm fairly confident (about 85%). Whether other products are affected is still open.
